caption: What if every cockroach on Earth vanished? Scientists know about 4,600 cockroach species, but only about 30 live around people and just 4 are the real kitchen pests. Roach-like insects first appeared around 320 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs. In forests, most cockroaches eat dead leaves and rotting plants, and their droppings return nitrogen to the soil that plants need. Birds, mice and rats eat them, so fewer roaches could mean fewer rodents and hungrier cats, snakes and hawks. Some parasitic wasps lay their eggs only in cockroach eggs, and they would almost certainly disappear too. The plot twist: scientists now classify termites as cockroaches, so every termite would vanish as well, and one termite colony can hold up to 3 million of them. Would YOU miss the roaches? 👇
